rows.what the ink shows: A small left loop leads into a long descending stroke and a low right arch; a detached raised dot sits above a tiny baseline mark, followed by a compressed almost horizontal terminal. The raised mark could be an i dot, but its lower stroke is not legible enough to establish puis; the isolated mark before (2) has no distinguishable a body or accent, and the compressed strokes do not establish grâce à either.

Two baseline A bodies are visible before B, including the lower opening of the second A beneath the tall cancellation. The raised sign has a forked top and closed lower loop, repeated in the same-line raised comparator; the inspected numeral 2 instead has an open bend and distinct rightward foot. This observed shape contrast supports * rather than 2.
